chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Bureyd al-Ijli, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the least of that which makes a servant a Mushrik. He said: The one who says for the kernel that it is a pebble, and for the pebble that it is a kernel, then makes a religion with it.

key_terms.النَّوَاة: The kernel or seed of a fruit
key_terms.دَانَ بِهِ: He submitted to it / made religion with it
key_terms.مُشْرِكاً: Polytheist, one who associates partners with God

ai.seo_question: What is the smallest act that constitutes Shirk according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies the minimal threshold of Shirk as the internal conviction and subsequent submission to an inanimate object, using the metaphor of confusing a seed with a stone to illustrate how trivial beliefs can become objects of worship. This definition highlights that Shirk is not limited to major deities but extends to any entity elevated to a status of divine authority or truth in the heart. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the intentionality and cognitive aspect of polytheism, where 'daining' (submitting) to the false attribution constitutes the core of the sin.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Bureyd Al Ijaly, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the least of that which makes a servant Mushrik’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who says for the kernel (grain) that it is a pebble, and for the pebble that it is a kernel, then makes a religion with it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from Burayd al-‘Ijli who has said the following: “Once I asked abu Ja’far (a.s.)

of the minimum amount of belief with which one is considered a polytheist (one who considers other things as partners of Allah). The narrator has said that the Imam said, ‘It is he who calls a nut a pebble and a pebble a nut and considers it his religion. ’”
